item.title: Presidential Message on National Recovery Month
item.description:
Briefings & StatementsPresidential Message on National Recovery MonthThe White HouseSeptember 2, 2026

Briefings & StatementsPresidential Message on National Recovery MonthThe White HouseSeptember 2, 2026
Briefings & Statements
The White HouseSeptember 2, 2026
During National Recovery Month, we celebrate the more than 23 million Americans who have found a pathway from addiction to recovery, we recognize those who have helped them reclaim their lives, and we renew our commitment to supporting those still struggling to find hope and healing.
Throughout every community in America, the effects of drug and alcohol addiction are felt in the lives of families, friends, and neighbors. Today, 48.4 million Americans suffer from addiction, and 69,973 Americans died last year to overdose. Every American deserves to live free from the grip of addiction—and my Administration is wholly committed to making that possible by preventing drug use before it starts, providing treatment at the earliest opportunity, and helping more Americans lead engaged and productive lives in recovery.
In January, I was proud to establish the Great American Recovery Initiative, coordinating a national response to the disease of addiction across government, healthcare, faith communities, and the private sector while fostering a culture that celebrates recovery. I also signed an Executive Order on Ending Crime and Disorder on America’s Streets to make our communities safer and help homeless Americans access addiction and mental health services needed to rebuild their lives. I am directing the Food and Drug Administration to prioritize non-opioid options for chronic pain, and I signed the SUPPORT for Patients and Communities Reauthorization Act to strengthen federal grant programs for treatment, overdose response, and mental health care. We are also stopping deadly drugs before they ever reach our shores. I signed the HALT Fentanyl Act into law, classifying all fentanyl-related substances as Schedule I drugs; formally designated major international drug cartels as foreign terrorist organizations; sealed our border; and empowered our brave Border Patrol and Armed Forces with the resources needed to carry out massive drug seizures to keep fentanyl off our streets.
Recovery is a testament to the strength of the American Spirit and the promise of a second chance. This month, we stand with those on the road to recovery and the families and communities who support them along the way. Together, we will help more Americans break free from addiction and lead healthy, productive, and fulfilling lives.

item.description:

The White HouseSeptember 2, 2026
This National Childhood Cancer Awareness Month, my Administration stands with the countless children facing the devastating effects of cancer. We recognize the love, strength, and care of the families who walk beside them through every step of their journeys. Above all, we commit to advancing lifesaving innovation and accelerating cures, giving every child the chance to live a long, healthy, and happy life.
American medicine has achieved remarkable breakthroughs in the fight to save the lives of our children, but cancer still remains the leading cause of death among children in the United States. To overcome such devastation, my Administration is strengthening preventative efforts, developing better treatments, and ultimately finding a cure to end this scourge.
Through the Make America Healthy Again Commission, we are addressing the root cause of chronic illnesses afflicting children—including cancer—and giving every child the chance to grow up healthy. We are also harnessing Artificial Intelligence to accelerate pediatric cancer research, identify promising solutions, and unlock new possibilities for prevention and cures. By bringing together American innovation and cutting-edge technology, we are providing new hope to children and families fighting cancer.
Every American child deserves the chance to grow up healthy and achieve their own unique American Dream. Together, we will fight to eradicate this vicious disease and build a future of greater hope, health, and possibility for America’s children.

item.title: Presidential Message on National Preparedness Month
item.description:
Briefings & StatementsPresidential Message on National Preparedness MonthThe White HouseSeptember 2, 2026

Briefings & Statements
The White HouseSeptember 2, 2026
America has always been a nation of strong, capable, and determined people who understand that strength must be built before crisis. Preparedness builds that strength, and readiness is the result. This National Preparedness Month, I call on every American citizen to ready themselves and their families, homes, businesses, and communities for natural and man-made threats.
Readiness begins with understanding the risks that matter most. Before a crisis, Americans can take practical steps to protect their homes and property, purchase affordable insurance against the risks they face, know evacuation routes, maintain an emergency kit with essential supplies, and stay informed through trusted local news and real-time alerts. These simple investments save lives, protect livelihoods, and help families and communities return to normal.
The same principle applies to the systems that power our Nation. American businesses and operators of critical infrastructure have an essential role and must also be ready. The energy, communications, transportation, financial, water, food, and health systems that power American life must remain available when we need them most. My Administration is working to strengthen the reliability of these systems, secure vital supply chains, reduce dangerous dependencies, and ensure services continue operating through crisis.
On June 23, 2026, I issued the National Resilience Strategy that articulates how the Nation, through federalism, will achieve a readiness posture. As President, my Administration continues transforming emergency management in the United States around readiness, responsibility, and results. States and communities must participate in this transformation by building their own fiscal and operational capacity to manage the emergencies they routinely face and support one another through mutual aid, drastically speeding up deployment and delivery of critical resources when disaster strikes. Americans deserve state and local governments that respond quickly to their needs, enabling communities to rebuild stronger and more resilient than ever before. This allows the Federal Government to concentrate its resources on the greatest risks and catastrophic incidents—regionally or nationally. It also makes our country harder to threaten. When America functions through crisis, our adversaries have fewer opportunities to harm us and fewer opportunities to achieve their objectives.
Strength begins with a Nation that is ready to act and such readiness is embodied by Americans who stand strong, who never back down, and who always put America First. This month, we honor our brave first responders, law enforcement officers, emergency personnel, and selfless volunteers. When the alarm sounds, they do not hesitate. They answer the call, protect their fellow Americans, and help keep our communities and our Nation safe and secure. Together, we resolve to build a more prepared, ready, and resilient America.

item.title: First Lady Melania Trump’s Personal Vision to Preserve America’s Story Through Superior Design
item.description:
Office of the First LadyFirst Lady Melania Trump’s Personal Vision to Preserve America’s Story Through Superior DesignThe White HouseSeptember 9, 2026
Office of the First LadyFirst Lady Melania Trump’s Personal Vision to Preserve America’s Story Through Superior DesignThe White HouseSeptember 9, 2026

Office of the First Lady
The White HouseSeptember 9, 2026
First Lady Melania Trump shared her forward-looking vision on the generational significance of institutional design, declaring that, “The White House stands as an architectural autobiography of America, embodying the enduring values of ambition, democracy, and civic life through its design, craftmanship, and the objects within.”
First Lady Melania Trump’s elevated creative vision has played a significant and meaningful role, shaping architecture, landscape, preserving historic interiors, and enhancing decorative arts to carry the White House forward.
First Lady Melania Trump’s most substantial design accomplishments include the award-winning design and construction of the White House Tennis Pavilion, the complete renovation of the Queens’ Bedroom and the Queens’ Bathroom, the conservation of the historic Zuber wall covering in the President’s Dining Room; and the 2020 restoration of the Rose Garden, which renewed its historic design while revamping infrastructure and accessibility. The First Lady affirmed that important design “fosters collaboration, conveys dignity, inspires ambition, and creates a sense of belonging to something larger.”
First Lady Melania Trump’s White House preservation work also encompassed the East Room floor, State Entrance and Hall marble floors, President’s Elevator, White House Bowling Alley, and Children’s Garden, all demonstrating a broader devotion to American craftsmanship and the preservation of the People’s House. Mrs. Trump highlighted, “Within the walls of the White House, these experiences become essential to our national identity.”
Notably, her design work has extended beyond the White House grounds to Camp David, further broadening her approach to preserving and evolving America’s historic presidential spaces. The First Lady exclaimed, “Great design transcends aesthetic appeal; it shapes our lived experiences.”
The First Lady’s comments were presented from the White House Rose Garden to honor the 2026 White House Historical Association Presidential Sites Summit. This convening brings together more than 200 leaders from presidential sites nationwide, reflecting on the America 250 celebration, with a view to the future.
The full remarks by First Lady Melania Trump are below.
The White House: America’s Architectural Autobiography
The White House stands as an architectural autobiography of America, embodying the enduring values of ambition, democracy, and civic life through its design, craftsmanship, and the objects within.
Generation after generation, America’s ideals and stories are woven directly into the fabric of the White House.
Design is a meticulous process that involves a multitude of choices—each line, texture, and play of natural light contributes to an overarching narrative. No detail is too small; what may seem insignificant today can influence how individuals connect with one another and perceive their place in history.
Within the walls of the White House, these experiences become essential to our national identity.
I encountered this truth firsthand when I sought to uncover the exquisite American War of Independence wallpaper designed by French artist Jean-Julien Deltil and created by the firm Jean Zuber and Co. This wallpaper was hidden behind the walls of the President’s Dining Room in the private Family Quarters. Created in 1852 and initially acquired by the Astor family, this exceptional piece was ultimately concealed beneath a wall treatment. My mission to restore and reveal it was driven by a commitment to preserving a vital piece of our American narrative. The successful unveiling of this work was not merely an act of restoration; it was an investment in the future of our nation’s story.
Great design transcends aesthetic appeal; it shapes our lived experiences.
It fosters collaboration, conveys dignity, inspires ambition, and creates a sense of belonging to something larger. This philosophy guided my work on the White House Tennis Pavilion, designed in collaboration with the Trust for the National Mall, the Executive Residence, and the National Park Service, and approved by the Committee for the Preservation of the White House, the Commission of Fine Arts, and the National Capital Planning Commission in 2018. Every detail was thoughtfully considered to ensure the new structure harmonized with the historic neoclassical character of the White House Grounds.

The White HouseSeptember 11, 2026
Melania and I send our warmest greetings to the entire Jewish community on Rosh Hashanah—the Jewish New Year and the first of the High Holy Days.
The Jewish community around the world marks the anniversary of when the Almighty created Adam and Eve and the story of humanity began. These two days open a solemn season of prayer, repentance, and spiritual renewal in preparation for Yom Kippur.
My Administration reaffirms our steadfast commitment to ushering in a historic renewal of faith across our country, eliminating the scourge of anti-Semitism, and defending the sacred right of religious liberty for every single American.
May you be inscribed in the Book of Life. Wishing you a Happy, Healthy, and Sweet New Year!

On Friday, September 11, 2026, the President signed into law:
H.R. 1276, which directs the Department of the Interior to remove all deed restriction from an approximately 3.62-acre parcel of land conveyed from the Department to the City of Paducah, Kentucky;
H.R. 2069, the “Stop Secret Spending Act of 2025,” which expands Federal spending transparency requirements to include other transaction agreements, and to modify related standards, oversight, and reporting;
H.R. 2196, the “National Emergency Medical Services Memorial Extension Act,” which extends the authority of the National Emergency Medical Services Memorial Foundation to establish a commemorative work on Federal lands in the District of Columbia to commemorate the commitment and service represented by emergency medical services personnel; and
H.R. 5366, the “Doug LaMalfa Federal Disaster Tax Relief Certainty Act,” which extends and codifies the Federal tax deduction for qualified disaster-related personal casualty losses and the exclusion from gross income of qualified wildfire relief payments.

item.title: Presidential Message on the Anniversary of the Battle of Fort McHenry
item.description:
Briefings & StatementsPresidential Message on the Anniversary of the Battle of Fort McHenryThe White HouseSeptember 13, 2026
Briefings & StatementsPresidential Message on the Anniversary of the Battle of Fort McHenryThe White HouseSeptember 13, 2026
Briefings & StatementsPresidential Message on the Anniversary of the Battle of Fort McHenryThe White HouseSeptember 13, 2026
Briefings & Statements
The White HouseSeptember 13, 2026
In September of 1814, 1,000 American patriots heroically defended our young Nation’s sovereignty at the Battle of Fort McHenry, where they halted the British invasion of Baltimore in a critical turning point in the War of 1812. Despite relentless cannon bombardment from the most powerful navy of its age, American forces stood strong. When dawn broke the next morning, the majestic Stars and Stripes remained proudly flying in full glory over the war-torn Fort McHenry.
The battle came at a perilous moment in our young Nation. British troops had stormed through the United States, setting fire to the White House and United States Capitol in a campaign to crush American willpower and restore British dominion over our hemisphere. After their attack on Washington, the British turned their sights north toward Baltimore with the aim of capturing one of America’s most vital seaports and forcing a surrender on their terms. With the future of our young Nation at stake, the citizens of Maryland rallied to arms, forming a militia and preparing their city for battle. Standing watch at Fort McHenry, these courageous soldiers and volunteers steeled themselves to defend the stronghold that guarded Baltimore Harbor.
On the morning of September 13, the British began their brutal naval assault on Fort McHenry, firing a barrage of exploding rockets and cannonballs. For 27 long, grueling hours, the American soldiers at Fort McHenry endured withering fire from the British fleet, but their unflinching resolve and masterful defenses saved the fort from destruction. Exhausted, frustrated, and dismayed, British troops abandoned their failed assault the next morning, sailing away in retreat.
Watching the battle unfold from a nearby ship, American lawyer Francis Scott Key feared the fort had succumbed to the British bombardment overnight. But when the dawn’s early light gleamed on the fort the next morning, Key’s anxious eyes beheld Old Glory gallantly streaming high in defiance and proudly signaling an American victory. Struck with a patriotic zeal, he immortalized America’s triumph that day by writing the most legendary ode to freedom ever put to paper: “The Star-Spangled Banner,” now enshrined as our National Anthem.
Two hundred and twelve years after this seminal battle, we honor the unwavering determination and persistence of the American forces that fought to preserve our Nation’s freedom at Fort McHenry. Their sacrifice and courage remind us that our freedom only endures through the tenacity and resolution of the patriots willing to defend it, both at home and abroad.
As we continue the work of saving our country, defending our values, reclaiming our sovereignty, and restoring our national pride—and as we reflect on 250 years of glorious American Independence—may the Star-Spangled Banner ever wave over the land of the free and the home of the brave.

item.title: First Lady Melania Trump’s Special Visit to Ashe County, North Carolina Bearing Witness to a Community’s Resilience
item.description:
Office of the First LadyFirst Lady Melania Trump’s Special Visit to Ashe County, North Carolina Bearing Witness to a Community’s ResilienceThe White HouseSeptember 15, 2026
Office of the First LadyFirst Lady Melania Trump’s Special Visit to Ashe County, North Carolina Bearing Witness to a Community’s ResilienceThe White HouseSeptember 15, 2026

Office of the First Lady
The White HouseSeptember 15, 2026
First Lady Melania Trump returned to North Carolina to visit Mountain View Elementary School in Ashe County, nearly two years after her initial visit to a community devastated by Hurricane Helene.
“True resilience means having the courage to look ahead and move society forward, creating a better future,” the First Lady said.
This visit shared a different story: one of resilience and a community determined to move forward. Mrs. Trump’s return denoted a new chapter in the western North Carolina regional recovery. Her first visit came in the immediate aftermath of the disaster, when the focus was on comforting survivors, thanking first responders, and confronting the extraordinary destruction left behind.
Mrs. Trump highlighted the forward-looking spirit of North Carolinians affected by Hurricane Helene, and their accelerated journey to the forefront of artificial intelligence technology.
Joining the First Lady at Mountain View Elementary was Carrie Robledo, a North Carolina second-grade teacher and 2026 Presidential AI Challenge National Champion. Mrs. Trump praised Ms. Robledo’s innovative work introducing young students to artificial intelligence.
“Ms. Robledo built something that no hurricane can destroy, and no flood can wash away: knowledge. And knowledge is power,” the First Lady said.
First Lady Melania Trump’s inaugural Presidential AI Challenge became the most expansive federally led artificial intelligence competition in American history, engaging more than 20,000 participants from all 50 states.
“That is the lasting spirit of America. We may face hard times, but we do not fail. We choose to grow—like a rare young flower pushing through the cold earth after a storm,” said the First Lady—celebrating the strength of a community that did not want to be defined by disaster and reflecting on Ashe County’s recovery.
Finally, The First Lady delighted students, teachers, and administrators with a special gift. BE BEST Fostering the Future, NVIDIA, and StudyFetch gifted 1,500 students AI Literacy training licenses and 100 Robotics Learning Kits powered by Jetson Nano. These new tools allow students to explore artificial intelligence and physical AI, develop technical skills, and bring their creative ideas to life.
The First Lady’s remarks, as prepared for delivery, are below.
North Carolina is the Definition of Resilience
Hello everyone and thank you for welcoming me back to North Carolina. It’s such an honor to meet the inspirational people from Ashe County and Mountain View Elementary School. I am so proud of you all.
To Dr. Cox, Mr. Graybeal, educators, students, administrators, and the brave families of Mountain View, thank you for welcoming me here today. Your story is incredible.
North Carolina is the definition of resilience.
Toughness in times of adversity is ingrained in the Tar Heel State’s character. It is easy to discover resilience within the courage of Ashe County’s families, the strength of this community, and the determination of its people to rise when needed.
Almost two years ago, Hurricane Helene hit North Carolina with incredible force. Record-breaking rainfall led your state legislature to describe it as “multiple 1,000-year flood events.” Hundreds of roads and bridges were damaged or destroyed. Over one million people lost power, and many neighborhoods lost water, communications, and other vital services. Including, Ashe County.
Tragically, 108 lives were lost.
For children here at Mountain View Elementary, the storm took away much more than just your daily routine. Your neighborhood was flooded and your school was transformed into a distribution center. For too many kids across the state, the familiar daily routines of classrooms, teachers, and friends were suddenly gone.
But, as the water levels rose, you stepped up for one another. Families welcomed others into their homes, brave individuals rushed toward the danger to assist, and faith leaders gave comfort.
Teachers became anchors of stability, and your school turned into more than a place to learn. It turned into a lifeline, providing food, water, supplies, counseling, and hope.
Mountain View’s Assistant Principal Cynthia Harless is an American hero. When Hurricane Helene struck, Cynthia drove to check on the school. Soon thereafter, floodwaters washed away the roads, leaving Cynthia and her family unable to return home. Rather than focus ...
